question: A 3-week-old newborn is brought to the emergency department by his parents because of 4 episodes of vomiting that occurred that morning. The parents report that the vomit was yellowish-green with no blood in it. The patient was born at 38 weeks' gestation via vaginal delivery and has generally been healthy. He has passed normal stools each day. There is no family history of serious illness. He appears irritable and pale. His temperature is 37.0°C (98.6°F), pulse is 146/min, and blood pressure is 90/55 mm Hg. Examination shows a soft, mildly distended abdomen with no masses or organomegaly. A nasogastric tube is inserted and intravenous fluid resuscitation is initiated. An x-ray shows no gas distal to the duodenum. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Yellowish-green vomit" -> "suggests bile" -> "possible intestinal obstruction" -> "x-ray shows no gas distal to duodenum" -> "suggests duodenal obstruction" -> "upper gastrointestinal contrast series to confirm" -> 85%

CHAIN: "3-week-old newborn" -> "bilious vomiting" -> "intestinal obstruction likely" -> "x-ray shows no gas distal to duodenum" -> "possible malrotation with volvulus" -> "upper gastrointestinal contrast series to assess" -> 80%
CHAIN: "Bilious vomiting" -> "intestinal obstruction" -> "x-ray findings" -> "no gas distal to duodenum" -> "upper GI series to identify level of obstruction" -> 75%
CHAIN: "Newborn with bilious vomiting" -> "intestinal obstruction suspected" -> "x-ray shows no gas beyond duodenum" -> "upper GI series to evaluate for malrotation" -> 70%
enhanced_information: The presentation of a 3-week-old newborn with bilious vomiting and an x-ray showing no gas distal to the duodenum suggests a high likelihood of intestinal obstruction, potentially due to malrotation with volvulus. Standard medical consensus indicates that an upper gastrointestinal (GI) contrast series is the most appropriate next step to confirm the diagnosis and assess the level of obstruction. This aligns with the retrieved evidence paths, which associate duodenal obstruction with the need for a GI series to evaluate the condition. Other options, such as laparoscopy or exploratory laparotomy, are more invasive and typically considered after imaging confirms the diagnosis. Abdominal ultrasound and flexible sigmoidoscopy are not appropriate for evaluating duodenal obstruction in this context. Therefore, the upper GI contrast series is the best next step in management.
analysis: The clinical presentation of a 3-week-old newborn with bilious vomiting and an x-ray showing no gas distal to the duodenum is highly suggestive of a bowel obstruction, likely due to malrotation with volvulus. In such cases, the standard medical approach is to perform an upper gastrointestinal (GI) contrast series. This imaging study helps confirm the diagnosis by visualizing the position of the duodenum and the presence of any obstruction or volvulus. While emergent exploratory laparotomy is a consideration if the patient is unstable or if imaging is unavailable, the current scenario does not indicate immediate surgical intervention without further diagnostic confirmation. Laparoscopy, abdominal ultrasound, and flexible sigmoidoscopy are not appropriate first-line diagnostic tools for this condition. Therefore, the upper GI contrast series is the most appropriate next step in management.
